why: A single-shop florist with about €25k monthly revenue, around 1,500 orders and margins of 16.3% and 9.1% that match revenue minus costs is believable.

A city employment service with 72k jobseekers (bands sum to 72k), 214,000 appointments at £40 plus £6.1m fixed cost gives about £200 per jobseeker, and per-person cost falls from Group A to E as stated.
Mining output growth ranging from -14.1% to 11.6% across five years and ordinal risk scores are believable country indicators.
Agrona's 375-391 thousand tonnes of nitrogen against a 2.2-3.15 million tonne market (about 12-17% share) and roughly 24% of phosphate are believable.
Coated glass rising from $7.85 to $21.20 per square metre through coating, distribution and cutting, with the waterfall adding up, is believable for a window maker.
Per-capita chip consumption of about 1.5-3 kg a year, bag sizes of 20-100 g and prices of $0.30-$1.40 above costs are believable.
A suburban driving school giving about 900 lessons a month at roughly €43 each, with margins of 12.6% and 9.7% that match revenue minus costs, is believable.
160,000 visits from 130,000 people with seven-tenths coming once leaves 91,000 single visits and 69,000 visits for 39,000 repeat visitors, who need at least 78,000, so the figures cannot all hold.
600,000 paying players with 1-7 purchases worth $14-$85 in 90 days and low one-year profit values of $0.30-$15 are believable for a mobile game after platform fees and costs.
A removals firm whose jobs double into the peak week and then drop, with casual mover hours always below total hours, is believable.
